subject: Co-term accelerator & surge capacity trigger plan
messages:
From: Lisa Nguyen <lisa.nguyen@acme.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: acme-procurement@acme.com
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion — term options + ramping capacity

David —

Thanks for the chat last week. We're starting to formalize our renewal and want to understand a few options before we put anything into procurement. High level asks:

- Can Redwood run a 3-year pricing scenario (multi-year) with an annual ramp schedule instead of an immediate capacity commit? We'll likely be at ~50% of projected tokens in Y1 and ramp to ~100% by Y3.
- We need clarity on auto-renew mechanics and how to opt out if usage materially changes.
- Co-terming with our other AI contracts is helpful for finance — can you align renewal dates and provide a co-term price?
- Procurement will want an explicit mid-term capacity review and the ability to top-up commit (not full renegotiation).

Can you send a straw proposal and indicate any legal guardrails (auto-renew notice window, SLO credit triggers, exit rights)? Procurement is on cc for visibility.

Thanks,
Lisa Nguyen
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Corp

---
Attachments: none
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Nguyen <lisa.nguyen@acme.com>
Cc: acme-procurement@acme.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — term options + ramping capacity

Lisa —

Appreciate the clear list. Attached is a concise straw proposal (RWD_Acme_Renewal_Proposal_2026.pdf) — key highlights here so procurement has the bullet version: 

- Commercial proposal: 36-month term, co-term to Acme FY (ends 2029-06-30). 20% list discount on hosted API unit price; additional 5% for annual prepay.
- Ramp schedule (committed capacity measured in token-equivalent units): Y1 = 50% baseline commit, Y2 = 75%, Y3 = 100%. Each year we evaluate actual consumption against commit for true-up.
- Surge / top-up: On-demand burst allowed up to 2x of committed capacity with usage billed at overage rate. Optional scheduled top-ups (quarterly) to convert burst into committed capacity.
- Mid-term review: Formal capacity review at the 12- and 24-month marks; mutual right to propose a top-up or reslice the ramp.
- Auto-renew: At the end of the 36-month term, auto-renew for 12 months unless either party gives 60 days' written notice. Karhtik, propose we limit automatic renewal to a single 12-month renewal to avoid perpetual renewals.
- Exit/credits: SLA credit ladder tied to p50/p90 latency targets and availability; legal to propose a capped remediation schedule rather than termination except in material breach.

I've looped in Marissa (AM) to own commercial onboarding and Karhtik (contracts) for the legal framing. If you want, we can run a short 30-minute workshop this week to walk procurement and engineering through the ramp mechanics and the top-up flow.

Next steps I suggest: 1) confirm co-term end date, 2) procurement returns redlines, 3) we slot a 30-min workshop.

Regards,
David Kim
Senior Sales Manager
Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: RWD_Acme_Renewal_Proposal_2026.pdf (proposal, 3 pages)
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Acme — negotiation points and redline priorities (quick)

Team —

Summarizing Lisa/procurement's asks and our recommended playbook. Keep this tight for legal and AM ops: 

1) Auto-renew windows: they asked whether we can opt for auto-renew to simplify finance. I recommend: 60-day notice to opt-out, auto-renew limited to +12 months once (i.e., no automatic multi-cycle renewals). Karhtik: protect us on price resets and add a fair-market review if costs materially change.

2) Mid-term capacity review: Commit to formal reviews at 12/24 months. Operationally, we should include a template agenda (usage, forecast, headroom) and clear options: (a) convert burst into commit, (b) leave as on-demand overage, (c) trigger a true-up. Marissa: we will own the review cadence and create the template.

3) Ramp schedule / staggered billing: Keep Y1 partial commit to lower initial AR risk, with a rolling true-up. Ensure finance can co-term invoices; if they want calendar-year alignment, we can provide an invoice pro-ration schedule. Ops concern: ensure we can reserve capacity and autoscale within dedicated pools.

4) SLA and credits: Karhtik, propose capped credits (e.g., up to 25% of monthly invoice) and gradated thresholds. Avoid termination language except for repeated material breach.

5) DocuSign/Procurement asks: They like a fast-sign flow. If procurement pushes for fewer negotiation cycles, we should be comfortable with a commercial playbook that converts some negotiation items into an appendix (e.g., surge-topup mechanics) rather than changing core T&Cs.

I'll draft a short reply we can send back that incorporates those guardrails. Happy to take edits.

-David

David / team —

Thanks for the quick turn. Procurement reviewed the PDF and attached a redline (Acme_Redlines_2026.docx). High-level response: we like the 36-month structure with the staged ramp, but two asks before procurement can push to legal sign-off: 

1) Mid-term capacity governance: we need an explicit 30-day decision window after each review where Acme can elect to convert measured burst into committed capacity at the agreed price — this avoids surprise billing.
2) Auto-renew opt-out: 60 days is acceptable; procurement asks for a 30-day billing freeze option during the notice period if Acme is in the middle of a procurement cycle.

If you can accept those two items and incorporate the redline into a DocuSign envelope, we can get this to legal tomorrow. We also want the mid-term reviews operationalized as a standing calendar invite with an agenda and data exports (usage + prefix caching metrics) sent 5 days before the review.

We'll attach the redline and a short procurement checklist in the docx. Please let me know how fast you can update.

Best,
Tim Sellers
CTO, Acme Corp
